cards.text: Paul, the apostle, is still writing to the church in Corinth about tongues and prophecy. Now he asks, "What then shall we say, brothers?" When they come together, everyone brings something: a psalm, a teaching, a revelation, a tongue or an interpretation.

cards.question: Everybody in Corinth shows up with a psalm, a teaching, a tongue or something else. What does Paul say all of it must do?

cards.text: First up: speaking in tongues, and Paul puts a NUMBER on it. Good, because the whole room going at once isn't a meeting, friend, it's a group chat with ninety-nine unread messages.

cards.question: In a meeting, ___ or at most ___ people should speak in a tongue, taking turns.
The people speaking in a tongue in Corinth take turns. What else does Paul say must happen?

cards.text: But what if nobody in the room can interpret? Paul's got a plan for that too.

cards.question: True or false: in Corinth, when there's no interpreter, Paul says the one with a tongue should speak up anyway.

cards.text: With no interpreter, he stays silent in the church and speaks only to himself and God. Next come the prophets, and two or three of them should speak.

cards.question: Two or three prophets speak in the Corinthian meeting. What should everyone else do?

cards.text: Now picture a prophet mid-message, and suddenly someone sitting down gets a revelation. This is the work meeting where two people start talking at once and then do the "no, YOU go" dance for ten straight minutes.

cards.question: A prophet in Corinth is speaking, and a revelation comes to someone seated. What does Paul say should happen?
True or false: Paul tells the Corinthians that only a chosen few of them can prophesy.
Prophesying in turn means everyone in the Corinthian church can be instructed and ___.

cards.text: Then Paul says, "The spirits of prophets are subject to prophets." I take that to mean a prophet can hold it and wait his turn, which is more than I can say for me standing next to a tray of warm cookies.

cards.question: Paul gives the reason for all these turns: God is not a God of ___, but of peace.
True or false: Paul says this way of peace is something only the church in Corinth has.

cards.text: Next, Paul writes, "Women are to be silent in the churches." He says they are not permitted to speak but must be in submission, as the law says, and if they want to ask about something, they should ask their own husbands at home.
Then Paul asks Corinth two questions: "Did the word of God originate with you? Or are you the only ones it has reached?" Whew, friend, Paul is NOT whispering.

cards.question: Paul says anyone in Corinth who thinks he's a prophet or spiritual should acknowledge something about what Paul is writing. What?

answers.text: It is just for this year

cards.question: If anyone ignores what Paul writes to Corinth, he himself will be ___.

cards.text: Now Paul wraps up everything he's said about tongues and prophecy with a "So, my brothers," and you know a wrap-up is coming. That's me at closing time, flour everywhere, saying "Okay, ONE more thing" for the fourth time.

cards.question: True or false: in his wrap-up, Paul tells the Corinthians to forbid speaking in tongues.
Paul tells his brothers in Corinth to be eager for one gift in particular. What is it?
Paul's last word to Corinth: everything must be done in a proper and ___ manner.

findings.problem: The question says "Everybody in Corinth shows up with a psalm, a teaching, a tongue." Verse 26 is about the church when it comes together ("When you come together, everyone has..."), not everybody in the city. This stretches the text. Something like "Everybody in the Corinthian church" would fit, the way card 13 words it.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: No story card sets up verse 31. The last setup the baker saw was card 8: "two or three of them should speak" (v29). That limit points a thoughtful baker toward True for "only a chosen few of them can prophesy." So the baker is led away from the answer instead of reasoning to it. Paul's earlier "Are all prophets?" (1 Cor 12:29) makes the statement even easier to argue. A story card should set up v31 (that they can all prophesy in turn), or the question should change.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: In the joke, Papa Dorin says "Okay, ONE more thing" for the fourth time, which is about a wrap-up that keeps dragging on. Paul's wrap-up in verses 39 and 40 is short and final. The comparison doesn't share the core action, and it suggests Paul keeps tacking things on. The card also says the same thing twice ("wraps up" and then "you know a wrap-up is coming").

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Verses 34 and 35 (women silent in the churches) are told on a single story card. They get no choice card, and the reason the text gives is left out ("for it is dishonorable for a woman to speak in the church"). The next card's joke, "Paul is NOT whispering," comes right after the card about silence, which may read as a nod to it. The docs say teaching gets choice cards "like anything else" and that the baker shouldn't miss an important detail. They also say "Not every moment needs a choice card," and they never say how to handle sensitive or much-debated verses.
findings.question: For sensitive or much-debated verses like 1 Corinthians 14:34–35, should Prep ask choice cards about them, tell them in full on a story card (including the reason the text gives), or keep them short as here? Should jokes stay off the cards right around them?
